subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Should authenticated Gateway plugin HTTP routes reject browser requests carrying an untrusted `Origin`, including trusted-proxy and explicit no-auth deployments, while continuing to allow non-browser requests that omit `Origin`?
rationale: The reported ACP files are not the relevant HTTP surface, and the correct policy must preserve trusted host automation while closing any browser-ambient authentication path; that security contract requires owner confirmation after a live reproduction.

options.title: Reject untrusted browser origins
options.body: Apply a shared or plugin-owned check that rejects requests with a present untrusted Origin but permits documented non-browser requests without Origin.

options.title: Restrict only admin HTTP RPC
options.body: Add the browser-origin check solely to `admin-http-rpc` after proving the issue does not affect other authenticated Gateway HTTP routes.

options.title: Document deployment constraints only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and rely on bearer authentication and private-ingress guidance if live testing proves browsers cannot reach an authenticated mutation path.

recommendation.title: Reject untrusted browser origins
recommendation.body: Apply a shared or plugin-owned check that rejects requests with a present untrusted Origin but permits documented non-browser requests without Origin.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest available history signal across Gateway configuration and security documentation and were explicitly routed this report.
